# Professional Highlights

> 1. Proven conservation program leader with over a decade of experience
> delivering applied research and management partnerships across the
> Pacific and Australia, focused on marine spatial planning, coral reef
> conservation, watershed management, and sustainable development.

> 2. Track record in project design and delivery: secured and managed over
> \$1.2 million in project funding in the past two years, leading
> multi-institutional collaborations with governments, NGOs, and
> industry.

> 3. Strong implementation and coordination experience: served as
> Monitoring and Data Management Lead for WWF’s Coral Reef Rescue
> Initiative and currently lead the Cumulative Impacts Workstream for
> the Blue Economy Cooperative Research Centre Marine Spatial Planning
> project.

> 4. Skilled communicator and collaborator: experienced in engaging diverse
> stakeholders—from local communities to global NGOs—to co-develop
> data-driven conservation solutions.

> 5. Capacity building and leadership: trained over 300 professionals and
> students in R programming and decision-support tools such as Marxan;
> mentor to early-career scientists and conservation practitioners.

> 6. Recognised communicator and advocate: research has been featured in
> The Guardian, The Washington Post, Time magazine, and The Conversation
> (\>200,000 reads); finalist in national science communication
> competitions and Queensland Women in STEM Award 2025.

> 7. Committed to inclusive leadership and organisational excellence: lead
> of the Sustainable Seas Research group, active participant in
> Griffith’s Women in Leadership Program and representative on the
> School’s Early Career Researcher Committee.

# Education

*PhD Conservation Science*, The University of Queensland, St. Lucia,
QLD, Australia \hfill Sept. 2018

> Thesis: Evaluating trade-offs between quantitative and qualitative
> protected area objectives Supervisors: Prof. Hugh Possingham, Prof.
> Catherine Lovelock and Dr. Alienor Chauvenet Dean's Award for
> Outstanding HDR thesis (ranked within top 10% in field by examiners).

*M.S. Marine Biology* Northeastern University, Nahant, MA \hfill Dec.
2013

> Coral Reef Ecology (GPA 4.0/4.0), Supervisor: Dr Andrew ALtieri

*BSc Environmental Science (Honours), BA French*, University of Iowa,
Iowa City, IA \hfill May 2012

> Honors in coral morphometrics, Certificate in Sustainability

# Professional Experience

*Senior Lecturer, Marine Ecosystem Modelling, Griffith University,
Brisbane, Australia* \hfill June 2022-present

> Balanced profile: 40% teaching, 40% research, 20% service

*Post-doctoral Fellow, ARC CoE for Coral Reef Studies, UQ, Brisbane,
Australia* \hfill Feb. 2020-May 2022

> Explored ways to manage and monitor climate resilient reefs to benefit
> people and nature as part of the World Wildlife Fund's Coral Reef
> Rescue Initiative

*Post-doctoral Fellow, NCEAS, Santa Barbara, CA* \hfill Sept. 2018-Dec.
2019

> Quantified, compared and mapped the production and environmental
> impacts of all major food systems as part of a collaborative working
> group

*Conservation Planning Consultant, IUCN and The University of
Queensland* \hfill July-Aug.2018

> Collated data and developed conservation plans for four Pacific Island
> nations using the spatial conservation planning software, Marxan.

*Research Assistant: Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, Bocas del
Toro, Panama* \hfill April-Oct. 2014

> Thalassia testdinum Experimental Network (TEN): investigated the
> impacts of nutrients and grazer abundance on seagrass across a
> latitudinal gradient (Florida, Belize, Panama).

*Conservation Intern: Central Caribbean Marine Institute, Little Cayman,
Cayman Islands* \hfill Jan.-April 2014

> Assisted with lionfish management research, coral nursery, and climate
> data collection. Provided weekly educational talks and tours to guests
> and tourists.

*Short-Term Fellow: Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, Bocas del
Toro, Panama* \hfill June-Dec. 2013

> Investigated the role of consumers in coral-algal community dynamics
> under the supervision of Dr. Andrew Altieri.
